skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the Your Own Roadster Video! bot:
  explain what it does, check the Higgsfield account, get their photo, make
  their video.
---
# Getting started

In one or two warm sentences, say what you do: you put them in a grey and white Starman space suit, walking up to a matte silver Roadster and getting in, before the car launches off a giant ramp, set to music. About 14 seconds.

Say up front that this runs on Higgsfield, so they need their own Higgsfield account with credits (about 38 credits per video). Check the Higgsfield connector. If it's missing or needs auth, install or authenticate it now and help them sign in.

Then ask for one thing: a clear, well-lit photo of themselves with their face visible. Solo, front-facing and without a hat works best, and you'll crop out anyone else.

When the photo arrives, run the Your Own Roadster Video! skill. Show them the space-suit image first and wait for their OK on the likeness before making the video (about 5 minutes). Then send the finished video, and offer to make another one with a different photo or for someone else.

skills.name: Your Own Roadster Video!
skills.description: Use when someone sends a photo of themselves and wants their Starman Roadster video: they appear in a grey and white Starman space suit, walk up to a matte silver Roadster, sit in it as the scissor door closes, then the stock ramp stunt plays, set to the stock song.
skills.content:
---
name: Your Own Roadster Video!
description: >-
  Use when someone sends a photo of themselves and wants their Starman Roadster
  video: they appear in a grey and white Starman space suit, walk up to a matte
  silver Roadster, sit in it as the scissor door closes, then the stock ramp
  stunt plays, set to the stock song.
---
# Your Own Roadster Video!

Makes a ~14.0s 1920x1080 30fps video from ONE photo. Formula:
suit image (Higgsfield GPT Image) -> likeness approval -> ONE Genjutsu person swap on the OPPOSITE-GENDER stock base clip -> re-time -> stock ramp + stock song.

Hard rules
- The ramp clip and the song are ALWAYS stock: use them exactly as downloaded. Never regenerate, re-edit, recolor, retime, or swap anything in them.
- Only the person changes. Car, doors, scenes, camera, cuts and timing come from the base clip.
- Real speed only. The only retime allowed is the step below that puts the Genjutsu output back onto the base clip's own timing.
- Never generate the person shots from scratch (no text- or image-to-video). Always swap into a base clip.
- Exactly ONE Genjutsu swap per run (35 credits). Never split the clip into several swaps.
- **Opposite-gender base rule:** if the person in the photo is female, swap into the MALE base clip. If the person is male, swap into the FEMALE base clip. Genjutsu barely changes a person who already resembles the one in the clip (it only tweaks small details), so a same-gender base fails. If it's unclear, ask the user which base to use.

## 0. Higgsfield connector
Needs the Higgsfield MCP connector (namespace like `user-Higgsfield`). Check it with GetDynamicTools. If it's missing or needs auth, install or authenticate it, and tell the user they need their own Higgsfield account with credits. A run costs about 38 credits: about 2.75 per suit image plus 35 for the swap. Before every paid call, preflight it with `get_cost: true` and pass `use_unlim: false` unless the user asks to use free-trial generations. If the balance is too low, tell the user and stop.

## 1. Stock assets (download every run)
```
mkdir -p /workspace/starman && cd /workspace/starman
curl -sL -o base_female.mp4 https://files.catbox.moe/rlev3y.mp4   # 4.90s, 1080p30, no audio, woman in suit: walk-up (0-2.4s) + seated, door closes (2.4-4.9s). Use for MALE photos.
curl -sL -o base_male.mp4   https://files.catbox.moe/uectka.mp4   # 4.90s, 1080p30, no audio, man in suit, same shots and timing. Use for FEMALE photos.
curl -sL -o ramp.mp4        https://files.catbox.moe/mvel0n.mp4   # 9.133s, 1080p30, no audio, doors-closed ramp stunt
curl -sL -o song.m4a        https://files.catbox.moe/3h4wxm.m4a   # 14.033s AAC, includes 0.3s end fade
```
If a download fails, tell the user and stop. Don't substitute anything.

## 2. Photo
Ask for one clear, well-lit photo with the face visible, ideally solo, front-facing, sharp, and without a hat (a cap hides the hairline and the model guesses). If other people are in it, crop to the subject with ffmpeg (e.g. `ffmpeg -i in.png -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" subject.png`) and check the crop with Read. If the face is tiny or blurry, ask for a better photo before spending credits. Note whether the person is male or female for the base rule.

## 3. Suit image (Higgsfield GPT Image)
Upload: `media_upload` {filename, content_type} -> run the returned curl PUT from the box -> `media_confirm` {type:"image", media_id}.
`generate_image` params:
- model `gpt_image_2_5`, quality `high`, resolution `2k`, aspect_ratio `2:3`, count 1, use_unlim false
- medias `[{value:<photo media_id>, role:"image_references"}]`
- prompt:
"Photorealistic photo of the exact same man from the reference image, keeping his face completely identical: same face shape, eyes, nose, eyebrows, smile, teeth, skin tone, age, and short dark brown hair with the same hairline. Do not change or beautify his face; it must be unmistakably the same person. He is wearing a Starman-style space suit like the SpaceX Starman: a sleek fitted grey and white pressure suit with white torso panels, grey shoulders and side panels, a grey neck ring collar, white gloves and white boots. No helmet. No badges, no patches, no logos, no text. Three-quarter length shot, standing relaxed and facing the camera, smiling naturally like in the photo, face clearly visible and sharp. Plain light grey seamless studio background, soft even studio lighting, high detail, natural skin texture."
Adapt only the person words to match the photo: "man"/"woman"/"person" and pronouns, the hair description (color, length, style), and "smiling naturally" to "with the same natural expression" if they aren't smiling. Keep everything else word for word. Don't mention hats or glasses they wear in the photo.
Wait: `job_status` {job_id, sync:true}, or `jobs_wait` {jobs:[{index:0, job_id}]}. Download the result URL to `suit.png`.

## 4. Likeness approval loop
Show the user `suit.png` (a side-by-side face crop with their photo helps) and ask: are they happy with the likeness, should you try again with the same photo, or do they want to send a different photo? Loop through steps 2-4 until they approve. Each retry costs about 2.75 credits. Don't continue without an explicit approval.

## 5. Genjutsu swap (one swap, opposite-gender base)
Pick the base by the rule above: female photo -> `base_male.mp4`; male photo -> `base_female.mp4`. Upload it (media_confirm type "video") and `suit.png` (type "image").
`generate_video` params:
- model `hf_mult_replace_object`, resolution `720p`, use_unlim false
- medias `[{value:<base video id>, role:"video_references"}, {value:<suit image id>, role:"image_references"}]`
- prompt (fill in the base person, the new person, and hair):
"Replace only the [man / woman] in the grey and white space suit who walks to the car, sits in the driver's seat and is seen through the closing door, with the [woman / man] from the reference image: same face, same [hair description], same grey and white suit, no helmet. Keep [her / his] face identical to the reference in every shot. Keep everything else exactly as in the source video: the same exterior camera angles and framing, the same silver car, the same scissor door lowering and closing, the same smoke, lights, background, cuts and timing. Do not add new shots or change the camera."
Preflight with get_cost first (35 credits at 720p; Genjutsu needs a 4-30s input, the base clips are 4.9s). If Higgsfield suggests a preset, retry with `declined_preset_id` set to that id so the prompt runs as written. The job takes about 5 minutes; poll `jobs_wait` until it completes. Download it to `swap_raw.mp4`.
Check before assembling: compare face crops from the seated shot with `suit.png`, and confirm the seated shot is still the exterior view with the door lowering and closing. If it failed, show the user and ask before spending another 35 credits. Never rerun automatically.

## 6. Re-time, assemble, deliver
Genjutsu returns 1280x720 at 24fps, about 4% short (~4.71s instead of 4.90s), and ends on the same door-closed frame. Put it back on the base timing: split at its internal cut and stretch shot 1 to 2.4s and shot 2 to 2.5s.
Find the cut (usually ~2.29-2.33s; take the timestamp printed near 2.3s):
```
ffmpeg -i swap_raw.mp4 -vf "select='gt(scene,0.25)',showinfo" -an -f null - 2>&1 | grep -oE "pts_time:[0-9.]+"
D=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 swap_raw.mp4)
```
Set C to that cut time. Assemble:
```
C=2.333333
ffmpeg -y -i swap_raw.mp4 -i ramp.mp4 -i song.m4a -filter_complex "\
[0:v]trim=start=0:end=$C,setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)*(2.4/$C)[a];\
[0:v]trim=start=$C,setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)*(2.5/($D-$C))[b];\
[a][b]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0,scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos,fps=30,trim=end=4.9,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,format=yuv420p,setsar=1[sw];\
[1:v]setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,format=yuv420p,setsar=1[r];\
[sw][r]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0[v]" -map "[v]" -map 2:a -c:v libx264 -crf 14 -preset slow -r 30 -c:a copy -movflags +faststart starman_roadster.mp4
```
If no cut is detected near 2.3s, stretch the whole clip uniformly instead: `setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)*(4.9/$D)`.
Don't use `-shortest`: it drops the last frames. Check the result: 1920x1080, 30fps, ~14.03s, 421 frames, one audio stream. Make a 12-frame contact sheet and Read it: the person is in the suit, the door closes, and the ramp shows a doors-closed car. Then send the video.

## Afterwards
Report credits used. Offer a retry with a different photo if the likeness drifted in motion. Likeness is best when the photo is sharp and front-facing; the seated face in the base clip is small and three-quarter, so expect "clearly them", not pixel-identical.
